name: Infostealer-reported persona compartmentalization and interview tooling

attribution.legal_posture: Publisher research assessment; legal charge, conviction, and verified legal-identity status remain unestablished.

caveats: Canonical structured UTC publication date is March 3, 2026; March 2 is retained only as an index/local-date variant.
Defenders should treat virtual-camera use, inconsistent video/audio behavior and identity-verification anomalies as corroborating signals that require other evidence.
Retain the compartmentalization pattern and activity classes only; exclude account names, credentials, raw history, domains, ports, and wallet material.

The source calls the endpoint owner a suspected DPRK IT worker and infers a local Indonesian facilitator from shared-use patterns. The attribution and facilitator relationship are assessments rather than independently verified identities. Raw telemetry and all actionable artifacts were excluded.

statements: The compromised environment contained virtual-camera, screen-recording, and video-editing software that Hudson Rock assessed as supporting pre-recorded or synthetic video during remote interviews and proof-of-work demonstrations.

Hudson Rock reported multiple separated browser profiles used for distinct personas and service roles alongside professional development, hosting-administration, and crypto-platform-cloning activity. The combination suggests one shared environment supporting identity management, development, and fraud infrastructure.
